transcript_facts.fact: Patient is eight weeks old, corrected to ten weeks on Saturday.
Patient reports low mood, crying all the time, and anhedonia (doesn't enjoy anything).
Symptoms have been present for about six weeks, starting a few weeks after birth, and have not lifted.
Patient cannot sleep even when the baby is asleep and lies there worrying.
Patient experiences intrusive thoughts of dropping the baby down the stairs and avoids carrying him on the stairs.
Patient denies any urge or intention to harm Oscar.
Patient has passive suicidal ideation, thinking they would be better off without them, but states they wouldn't do anything.
Patient had previous depression at age 19, treated with fluoxetine for a year, and it helped.
Patient's mother had mental health issues, including hearing things, and had to be hospitalized after having the patient's brother.
Patient reports no current medications or known drug allergies.
Relative reports struggling and having had a couple of panic attacks at work.
Patient's PHQ-9 score is 17, which is consistent with moderately severe depression and postnatal depression.
Plan to start sertraline 50 milligrams once a day, noted as one of the safest antidepressants when breastfeeding.
Clinician plans to refer the patient to the perinatal mental health team and inform the health visitor.
Clinician will provide details for Talking Therapies, noting they prioritize new parents.
Safety-netting advice: Call 111 (mental health option) or 999 if suicidal thoughts worsen or safety is compromised.
